sentences.text: As described in Notes 2 and 3 to the consolidated financial statements, the Firm carries $1.5 trillion of its assets and $586.2 billion of its liabilities at fair value on a recurring basis.

Included in these balances are $10.9 billion of trading assets and $51.8 billion of liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis, collectively financial instruments, which are classified as level 3 as they contain one or more inputs to valuation which are unobservable and significant to their fair value measurement.

As described in Notes 1 and 20 to the consolidated financial statements, the Corporation carries certain financial instruments at fair value, which includes $10.0 billion of assets and $6.3 billion of liabilities classified as Level 3 fair value measurements that are valued on a recurring basis and $3.1 billion of assets classified as Level 3 fair value measurements that are valued on a nonrecurring basis, for which the determination of fair value requires significant management judgment or estimation.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, the Company carried $20.4 billion in financial assets and $25.7 billion in financial liabilities classified as Level 3, valued using significant unobservable inputs such as market multiples, discount rates, and capitalization rates. The auditor identified the valuation of these instruments as a critical audit matter due to the significant judgment by management and the high degree of auditor subjectivity and effort required to evaluate the unobservable inputs.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS identify Level 3 financial instruments as a critical audit matter due to the use of significant unobservable inputs. JPM lists inputs such as interest rate volatility and equity volatility, while GS lists market multiples, discount rates, and correlation. Both disclosures quantify the Level 3 balances: JPM identifies $10.9 billion in assets and $51.8 billion in liabilities, while GS identifies $20.4 billion in assets and $25.7 billion in liabilities.

sentences.text: Included in these balances are $10.9 billion of trading assets and $51.8 billion of liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis, collectively financial instruments, which are classified as level 3 as they contain one or more inputs to valuation which are unobservable and significant to their fair value measurement.

The unobservable inputs used by management to estimate the fair value of certain of these financial instruments include interest rate volatility, equity volatility, Bermudan switch value and correlation relating to interest rates, interest rate-to-foreign exchange, equity prices, equity-to-foreign exchange and equity-to-interest rate.

As described in Notes 4 and 5 to the consolidated financial statements, as of December 31, 2024, the Company carries financial instruments at fair value, which includes $20.4 billion of financial assets and $25.7 billion of financial liabilities classified in level 3 of the fair value hierarchy (a portion of which relates to certain equity securities and hybrid financial instruments), as one or more inputs to the financial instrument's valuation technique are significant and unobservable.

Significant unobservable inputs used by management to value certain of the level 3 financial instruments included market multiples, discount rates, and capitalization rates for equity securities; and correlation and volatility for hybrid financial instruments.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm carries material Level 3 financial instruments with limited price transparency, including $6.8 billion in assets and $4.1 billion in liabilities carried at fair value on a recurring basis, plus $6.1 billion in Level 3 loans held for sale as of December 31, 2024. The audit of these items was identified as a critical audit matter due to the subjectivity, use of unobservable inputs, and complex proprietary models involved in their valuation.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and MS report the recurring fair value of Level 3 assets and liabilities and highlight the subjectivity and use of unobservable inputs. JPM reports $10.9 billion in assets and $51.8 billion in liabilities using internally developed models and unobservable inputs like volatility. MS reports $6.8 billion in assets and $4.1 billion in liabilities, noting that the valuation is inherently subjective and involves proprietary models with unobservable inputs.

sentences.text: Included in these balances are $10.9 billion of trading assets and $51.8 billion of liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis, collectively financial instruments, which are classified as level 3 as they contain one or more inputs to valuation which are unobservable and significant to their fair value measurement.
The Firm utilized internally developed valuation models and unobservable inputs to estimate fair value of the level 3 financial instruments.

As described in Note 4, these Level 3 financial assets and liabilities carried at fair value on a recurring basis approximate $6.8 billion and $4.1 billion, respectively, and the Level 3 loans held for sale approximate $6.1 billion at December 31, 2024.

Unlike financial instruments whose inputs are readily observable and, therefore, more easily independently corroborated, the valuation of these financial instruments is inherently subjective and often involves the use of unobservable inputs and proprietary valuation models whose underlying algorithms and valuation methodologies are complex.
